scenes.heading: SCD Type 2
scenes.narration: A Slowly Changing Dimension of Type 2 preserves full history by adding a new row for every change.

scenes.heading: How Type 2 tracks history
bullets: Each change inserts a new versioned row.
Effective-from and effective-to dates bound each version.
A current flag marks the active row.
Facts join to the version valid at event time.
scenes.narration: When an attribute changes, Type 2 closes the old row and inserts a fresh one. Effective date ranges record exactly when each version was valid, and a current flag identifies the live one. This lets a sale join to the customer's address as it was on the day of purchase, not today.

scenes.heading: Closing old and inserting new
scenes.code:
-- expire the current version
UPDATE dim_customer
SET    effective_to = CURRENT_DATE, is_current = FALSE
WHERE  customer_id = 'C100' AND is_current = TRUE;

-- insert the new version
INSERT INTO dim_customer
  (customer_id, city, effective_from, effective_to, is_current)
VALUES
  ('C100', 'Austin', CURRENT_DATE, '9999-12-31', TRUE);
scenes.narration: The first statement stamps the old row with an end date and clears its current flag. The second inserts the new version, open-ended until it too changes. Together they preserve a complete timeline, so historical reports stay accurate to the moment they describe.

scenes.heading: Serving a Type 2 lookup
steps: Point new facts at the new key
scenes.narration: Each incoming record is compared against the current version in the dimension. If nothing changed, you leave it alone; if something did, you expire the old row and add a new one. New facts then reference the freshly created surrogate key.

scenes.text: SCD Type 2 keeps a full versioned history with date ranges and a current flag, so you can analyze data as it was at any point in time.
scenes.narration: Type 2 is the workhorse for tracking meaningful change, because it lets the past stay true even as the present moves on.
